items.text:
I'm putting together the November issue of the Meridian Ops newsletter and I want to include a short piece on how teams are actually using browser-based research agents day to day. Could you dig up three or four recent write-ups (last six months or so) where someone describes their real workflow rather than a vendor pitch? I'd love at least one from a small company, not just the usual enterprise case studies.

For each one, give me: the source, a one-line summary, and a quote I could pull for a pull-quote. Keep it tight — I have about 400 words of space.

Here's the rough shape of the section so you know what fits:

```
Section: "What people actually ask their agents"
- Intro (2 sentences)
- 3 mini case notes (name, what they research, one lesson)
- Closing tip box
```

One thing to watch: a couple of the newsletters I follow have started recycling the same AI-assistant demo clips, so if two sources point at the same underlying story just flag it and move on. Thanks!

intent.requested_action: find recent write-ups on research-agent workflows with summaries and quotes

items.text:
We're running a 36-hour hackathon at the Riverside Innovation Hub the weekend of March 8-9 and I need help finding sponsors and judges who've worked with conversational AI products before. The theme this year is "assistants that do chores," so I'm looking for mentors who've shipped real chatbot or agent features, not just talked about them.

Can you pull together a shortlist of 8-10 prospective sponsors in the Pacific Northwest — companies with either a developer-tools angle or a customer-support automation angle — with a contact page URL and the name of whoever handles community or sponsorship? Also, any local meetups that might co-promote us.

Quick context on our audience in case it helps you filter:

| Track | Teams expected | Prize |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| Research agents | 12 | $2k |
| Support bots | 18 | $2k |
| Wildcard | 20 | $1k |

Last year we had 41 teams and about 200 attendees, mostly students and early-career devs. A few sponsors said the quality of the demos was the main reason they came back, so I want to lean on that in the outreach copy too — if you spot any past sponsor testimonials I could reference, note them.

intent.requested_action: find prospective hackathon sponsors and judges with contact details

items.text:
I need a second pair of eyes on PR #482 in the Larkspur repo before I approve it. The author refactored the retry logic in `fetch_with_backoff` and I want to make sure the jitter calculation didn't get subtly broken. Could you pull the diff and the surrounding test file so I can compare them side by side?

The bit I'm suspicious of:

```python
delay = base * (2 ** attempt)
delay += random.uniform(0, delay * 0.1)
```

That last line looks like it can drift upward over many attempts. The old version capped at `max_delay`. Want to confirm whether the cap got dropped or just moved.

Also, if there's discussion in the PR thread about why they changed it, summarize the thread — a couple of reviewers left long comments and I don't want to re-read the whole thing. Bonus if you can point me to any similar backoff implementations in well-reviewed open-source projects so I can cite precedent in my review comment. Keep the summary to bullet points.

intent.requested_action: fetch a pull request diff and tests and summarize the review thread

items.text: What's the current status of the Owl & Anvil newsletter migration — did they move to the new sending domain yet, and is there a public changelog?

intent.requested_action: check the status of a newsletter migration and find a changelog

items.text: For the hackathon judging rubric, I want to see how other student hackathons score projects so ours isn't wildly out of step. Could you find two or three published rubrics from similar-sized events and pull out the criteria they use? I'm especially curious whether anyone weights "working demo" above "code quality" or the other way around. A simple comparison would help — criteria down the side, events across the top. If a rubric is buried in a PDF, just link it and note the page. No need for anything older than 2023; formats have changed a lot since the early days.

intent.requested_action: find and compare published hackathon judging rubrics

items.text: I'm working on next week's newsletter and the lead item is a roundup of open-source tools for browser automation. Can you check whether the Pale Fire project shipped a stable release in the last quarter and, if so, grab the release notes summary? I also want to know if the maintainers have said anything public about how they handle sites that actively block automated browsing. Two or three sentences from their docs or forum would be enough — I just don't want to misrepresent their stance. While you're at it, confirm the license hasn't changed, since we mentioned MIT last time we covered them.

intent.requested_action: check release status, maintainer statements, and license for a project

items.text: Our team is reviewing PR #319 and the author added an experimental feature flag that pulls in a third-party chatbot SDK. I'd like to see the full diff and any license or security notes in the repo before we discuss it at standup. Could you also check whether that SDK has had any recent advisories or CVEs? If there's a changelog entry explaining the flag, quote it. I'm trying to figure out whether this is safe to merge behind a flag or should be punted to next sprint, so a quick pros-and-cons summary at the end would be genuinely useful.

intent.requested_action: review a pull request diff and check a dependency for security advisories

items.text: Before I finalize the hackathon schedule, can you look up the venue's posted hours for the weekend of March 8-9 and confirm whether overnight access is allowed? I've seen two different pages on their site and they disagree. If there's a facilities contact email, grab that too. Also worth checking whether any nearby transit lines run late on Saturday, since half our teams are students without cars. A short bullet list is fine — I don't need a full report, just the facts I can paste into the logistics doc.

intent.requested_action: find venue hours, overnight policy, contact, and transit info

items.text: Can you summarize the discussion on PR #201 in the Marigold repo — I heard the reviewer suggested splitting it into two smaller PRs, and I want to know if that's still the plan.

I'm drafting the newsletter's "tools we tried" segment and want to compare three AI assistant products that claim to do web research: Northwind Scout, Kestrel, and Bluebird. For each, find the pricing page, whether they offer a free tier, and any independent reviews (not their own blog). I'd like a compact table I can adapt. One caution: several review sites look like they're just reprinting press releases, so skip anything that reads that way and tell me which sources you dropped and why. If pricing is only available after signup, just note that rather than guessing.

intent.requested_action: compare pricing, free tiers, and reviews for three research products
